text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Japan has signed an agreement to provide $2 billion in official development aid for the development of electricity in Vietnam. The funds will be used for the construction of power plants and transmission networks.
-- An estimated 3,000 people packed Hanoi's new Daewoo Hotel last night for a gala extravaganza celebrating the official opening of the capital's first five-star hotel.
-- Six people died and more than 2,000 hectares of paddy field and many houses were inundated following flash flood in the central coast province of Quang Nam-Da Nang.
-- National Assembly delegates have raised concern that agricultural land area has fallen as a result of industrialization.
-- Vietnam has officially established diplomatic relation with the Solomon Islands.

-- Torrential rains in the last few days have caused serious flooding in Vietnam's southwestern provinces of Minh Hai, Tien Giang and Vinh Long. So far, flooding in the Mekong Delta has caused damage worth $126 million.
